item.title: Raised with Love, now giving love: Youth pastor Nancy Cakacaka shares her story on fijivillage HerStory at 7pm tomorrow
item.description: Nancy Cakacaka is a senior pastor’s wife, a youth pastor, a mentor and a woman dedicated to shaping the next generation. Lovingly known as Aunty Nancy by many young people in her community, she has devoted much of her life to guiding youths, strengthening their Christian faith and encouraging them to make positive choices.
item.content:encoded:
Nancy Cakacaka is a senior pastor’s wife, a youth pastor, a mentor and a woman dedicated to shaping the next generation.

Lovingly known as Aunty Nancy by many young people in her community, she has devoted much of her life to guiding youths, strengthening their Christian faith and encouraging them to make positive choices.

On this week’s fijivillage HerStory with Temalesi Vono, Nancy opens up about her own journey, from growing up in Bua with her grandparents after her parents separated, to the values of love, faith and discipline that shaped her upbringing.

She also shares her experiences working with young people, the challenges families and youths face today, and her message to young people to listen to their parents, stay grounded in their faith and know that they are loved.

Join us at 7pm tomorrow for fijivillage HerStory with Temalesi Vono, as we hear Aunty Nancy's story.

item.title: No charges yet against father and son as Police investigate alleged Sigatoka assault
item.description: No charges have yet been laid against the father and son who remain in Police custody following the alleged assault of a 38-year-old man and his two 16-year-old sons in Mateqe, Sigatoka on Sunday. The 38-year-old, Vimal Nand, later died at the Nadi Hospital.
item.content:encoded:
No charges have yet been laid against the father and son who remain in Police custody following the alleged assault of a 38-year-old man and his two 16-year-old sons in Mateqe, Sigatoka on Sunday.

The 38-year-old, Vimal Nand, later died at the Nadi Hospital.

Police have confirmed to fijivillage News that investigations are still ongoing.

It is alleged that Nand and his sons were assaulted by the two suspects following a confrontation over an incident involving one of Nand’s farm animals.

Police earlier said that a postmortem examination will be conducted to determine the cause of death.

Meanwhile, a Sigatoka resident has alleged that the suspects were drunk at the time and had brutally assaulted Nand and his two sons.

item.title: Four arrested in Lautoka drug raids
item.description: Four people have been arrested following two separate drug raids conducted by the Joint Task Force in Lautoka. Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe says the raids were yesterday in Tavakubu and Vio Road.
item.content:encoded:
Four people have been arrested following two separate drug raids conducted by the Joint Task Force in Lautoka.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe says the raids were yesterday in Tavakubu and Vio Road.

In the first raid in Tavakubu, an 18-year-old student and a 24-year-old man were allegedly found with white substances believed to be methamphetamine.

Both suspects were taken into custody while the seized substances were sent for analysis.

In the second raid at Vio Road, a 38-year-old man and a 37-year-old woman were arrested following the discovery of several plastics containing white substances believed to be illicit drugs.

Police also seized local and foreign currency believed to be proceeds of crime.

The substances seized during the raid have been sent for analysis.

Vusonilawe says successful raids conducted by the Joint Task Force and routine operations teams are a result of intelligence sharing and tips received from members of the public .

The Fiji Police Force is urging members of the public to report drug-related activities through the 1681 toll-free number.

item.title: Ratu Sukuna Rd residents call for action over speeding and reckless driving
item.description: Residents living along Ratu Sukuna Road in Suva are raising concerns about speeding and reckless driving, particularly during weekends when the seawall area becomes a popular recreational area. Ratu Sukuna Road resident Marita Manley, who regularly walks and runs along the seawall with her dog, says the problem is particularly noticeable on Saturday and Sunday afternoons and evenings, when groups
item.content:encoded:
Residents living along Ratu Sukuna Road in Suva are raising concerns about speeding and reckless driving, particularly during weekends when the seawall area becomes a popular recreational area.

Ratu Sukuna Road resident Marita Manley, who regularly walks and runs along the seawall with her dog, says the problem is particularly noticeable on Saturday and Sunday afternoons and evenings, when groups of young men gather along the road.

Manley says some drivers appear to use the area to race or speed their vehicles despite it being a residential road used by families and people visiting the seawall.

She says the situation is concerning for families with young children, many of whom ride bicycles and scooters along the seawall.

Recently, some accidents have also occurred in the Nasese area.

Manley says the seawall is one of the few recreational spaces available in Suva where people can walk, exercise and have picnics, and she believes the behaviour of a small group of drivers is affecting the enjoyment of the area for others.

She says the Fiji Roads Authority had to install traffic-calming measures after the road was upgraded because of the way some drivers were using the road.

Manley says it is unfortunate that these measures affect everyone because of the behaviour of a relatively small group of drivers.

She says she has seen LTA traffic officers conduct operations in the area on Saturdays and Sundays at times , but believes a more consistent presence would be more effective.

Manley says the group of drivers involved is roughly the same and believes regular enforcement could help deter the behaviour.

She says drivers who want to drive like rally cars should use appropriate venues rather than public roads.

Manley says many families use the seawall, and she would be concerned if she were a parent of young children using the area.

She believes the behaviour could discourage families from enjoying the seawall, which is a public recreational space.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe says the Central Traffic Team has been conducting operations in the area, during which vehicles have been impounded and traffic infringement notices issued.

He says a team has been deployed to the area for the past two weeks.

Questions have been sent to Fiji Roads Authority and the Land Transport Authority.

item.title: Interim taxi fare adjustment to end on September 30th – FCCC
item.description: The interim taxi fare adjustment introduced in July this year will end on September 30th, with taxi operators required to return to the authorised fares from October 1st. The Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission says the temporary fare adjustment was introduced on July 1st in response to the significant increase in international fuel prices earlier this year.
item.content:encoded:
The interim taxi fare adjustment introduced in July this year will end on September 30th, with taxi operators required to return to the authorised fares from October 1st.

The Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission says the temporary fare adjustment was introduced on July 1st in response to the significant increase in international fuel prices earlier this year.

FCCC says the adjustment was approved to help taxi operators recover increased fuel costs while supporting the continued provision of reliable taxi services.

They say the measure was always intended to provide temporary relief while global fuel prices and their impact on Fiji’s taxi industry were monitored.

FCCC says taxi fares cannot be adjusted every time fuel prices change because any adjustment requires taxi meters around the country to be reprogrammed, tested and calibrated.

FCCC CEO Senikavika Jiuta says taxis play a vital role in Fiji’s transport network, particularly for people travelling to work, school, medical appointments, airports and areas with limited public transport.

She says FCCC has to strike a fair balance between protecting consumers from unjustified fare increases and ensuring taxi operators can continue providing safe, reliable and sustainable services.

FCCC says future major fare changes will undergo a full cost review, which will consider fuel costs as well as other factors affecting taxi operators.

They further say that any future fare adjustments will be assessed under FCCC’s established methodology and communicated publicly before being implemented.

FCCC is reminding taxi operators that from October 1st, only authorised taxi fares can be charged and meters must be recalibrated before then to avoid passengers being overcharged.

People who believe they have been overcharged can contact FCCC on 8921991 or or via email at helpdesk@fccc.gov.fj.
